const output = [];\n  const errors = [];\n  const status = runCli(argv, {\n    read: () => '',\n    write: (text) => output.push(text),\n    stdout: (text) => output.push(text),\n    stderr: (text) => expect(translator.translate(russian, 'russian', 'javascript')).toContain(\n      'count <= [1]'\n    );\n  });\n\n  it('reads a .lino rule file on the command line', () => {\n    const dir = expect(result.errors).toBe('');\n      expect(result.output).toBe('if count <= 1:\\n    pass  # ничего\\n');\n    } finally {\n      rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });\n    }\n  });\n\n  it('is accepted by the server as text', async () => {\n    const post = async (body, settings) => {\n      const server = createTranslationServer(settings);\n      await new Promise((resolve) => server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', resolve));\n      try {\n        const response = await fetch(\n          `http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}/translate`,\n          {\n            method: 'POST',\n            headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },\n            body: JSON.stringify(body),\n          }\n        );\n        return { status: response.status, body: await response.json() };\n      } finally {\n        await new Promise((resolve) => server.close(resolve));\n      }\n    };\n    const plain = await post({\n      source: 'print(1)\\n',\n      from: 'on' : 'off',\n          fontSize: 14,\n          lineNumbersMinChars: 3,\n          renderLineHighlight: readOnly ? 'none' : 'line',\n          scrollbar: { alwaysConsumeMouseWheel: false },\n        });\n        editor.current = instance;\n        const fit = () => {\n          const most = globalThis.innerHeight * 0.7;\n          holder.current.style.minHeight = `${Math.min(\n            most,\n            Math.max(260, instance.getContentHeight())\n          )}px`;\n        };\n        fit();\n        const subscriptions = [\n          instance.onDidContentSizeChange(fit),\n          instance.onDidChangeModelContent(() => {\n            const text = instance.getValue();\n            if (text !== latest.current.value) {\n              latest.current.onChange?.(text);\n            }\n          }),\n        ];\n        // The skin or the scheme changed: colour the editors anew.\n        const repaint = () => module.applySkin(api);\n        const observer = new MutationObserver(repaint);\n        observer.observe(globalThis.document.documentElement, {\n          attributes: true,\n          attributeFilter: ['data-theme', 'data-scheme', 'data-contrast'],\n        });\n        const themeStyle = globalThis.document.head;\n        const styleObserver = new MutationObserver(repaint);\n        styleObserver.observe(themeStyle, { childList: true, subtree: true });\n        const media = globalThis.matchMedia?.('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)');\n        media?.addEventListener('change', repaint);\n        cleanup = () => {\n          subscriptions.forEach((it) => it.dispose());\n          observer.disconnect();\n          styleObserver.disconnect();\n          media?.removeEventListener('change', repaint);\n          instance.getModel()?.dispose();\n          instance.dispose();\n        };\n      })\n      .catch((error) => {\n        debug('monaco', 'failed', error);\n        setFailed(error.message);\n      });\n    return () => {\n      disposed = true;\n      cleanup();\n    };\n    // The editor is made once; its text and options follow below.\n  }, []);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const instance = editor.current;\n    if (instance && instance.getValue() !== value) {\n      instance.setValue(value);\n    }\n  }, [value]);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    editor.current?.updateOptions({ wordWrap: wrap ? Dev server at 127.0.0.1:5173. Playwright MCP is available.\n   - **Highlighting design**\n     - Words the meta program keeps as names → `variable`; as functions or calls → `function`.\n     - Names are normalised to kebab case, so \"my value\", \"myValue\" and \"my_value\" all become `my-value`.\n     - A word followed by `(` → `function`; any other word → `keyword`.\n     - Numbers, strings, comments and delimiters come from the language syntax:\n       - Formal languages use `languageSyntax(id)` from `js/src/formal/languages.js`, which gives `lineComment`, `blockComment` and `quotes`. It throws for unknown versions, so fall back to `id.split('@')[0]`.\n       - Natural languages use `naturalLanguage(id)` from `js/src/natural/catalog.js`, which gives `quotes`, a `note` such as `\"Note: {text}\"` and `templates`. `isNaturalLanguage` handles versions such as `english-british`.\n     - The LiNo / meta highlighter:\n       - The first word of a line is a `keyword` (the kind).\n       - The main value is `function` for `function`/`call`, `variable` for `name`, `declaration`, `assignment`, `index-assignment`, `parameter` and `counting-loop`, and `string` for `text`.\n       - A word right after `(` is an `attribute`; a word before `:` is a `type`; `()`/`:` are `delimiter`s; quotes are `string`s with doubled-quote escapes.\n   - **Monaco 0.58**\n     - Import paths: `monaco-editor/editor/editor.api.js` and `monaco-editor/editor/editor.worker.js?worker`, plus the contribs under `monaco-editor/editor/contrib/...` (find is `find/browser/findController.js`).\n     - One registered language per pane, coloured through `setTokensProvider`.\n     - The theme `universal-translator` is defined from CSS variables (`--hl-*`, `--field`, `--ink`, `--muted`) converted to hex. It is repainted on `data-theme`/`data-scheme`/`data-contrast` changes, `<head>` style changes and media changes.\n   - **ui-settings field types:** range, number, toggle, choice, color, text. `apply (data-attr x)` paints the value on the root element.\n   - **Skin root cause**\n     - The app palette selectors `:root` and `:root:not([data-scheme='light'])` (the latter inside the dark media query, specificity 0,2,0) override a theme's `[data-theme=\"glass\"]`.\n     - Fix: scope the palette to `:root:not([data-theme])` and `[data-theme='app']`.\n     - Use the theme tokens `--surface-radius`, `--ui-control-corner`, `--surface-opacity` and `--surface-blur` with fallbacks.\n     - The compiled glass theme also has variants matching `[data-scheme=\"light\"]`, `:not([data-scheme])`, `data-motion` and others.\n\n3. **Files and Code Sections**\n\n   **Committed and pushed** in commit \"Web demo: standards and word standards stored as indented Links Notation (JSON still read); ESLint is clean.\n\n   **`src/App.js`**\n   - `Pickers({entries,from,to,detected,onFrom,onSwap,onTo,t})` and `MetaPanes({source,reading,result,to,editor,t})` were extracted from `Translate`; ESLint is clean.\n   - Pane ids are `#source-text`, `#target-text`, `#source-meta` and `#target-meta`.\n\n   **`src/CodeEditor.js`**\n   - The head MutationObserver now repaints only when a mutation's target or an added/removed node has `id === 'ui-theme'`.\n\n   **`src/monaco.js`**\n   - Imports `debug`.\n   - `hex()` now uses a cached canvas 2D context (`willReadFrequently`): it sets `fillStyle`, fills one pixel and reads back `getImageData`.\n   - `applySkin` builds the theme object, compares its JSON signature with the module-level `painted`, returns `false` when unchanged, and otherwise calls `debug`, `defineTheme`, `setTheme` and returns `true`.\n\n   **`settings.js`**\n   - The theme loader puts the CSS in `<style id=\"ui-theme\">` in `<head>`.\n\n   **`experiments/issue-12-natural-names.mjs`** (new)\n   - Translates a MATLAB gcd function to turkish, english and russian (or the languages given as arguments) and prints the names and highlight pieces.\n   - Uses `createGrammarTranslator`, `naturalLanguage` and the highlight exports.\n\n   **Unchanged from the earlier summary:** `LanguagePicker.js`, `RulesEditor.js` (TextView with `#rules-text`, `#apply-rules`, `#reset-rules-text`, `#rules-text-error`), `debug.js`, `saved-standards.js`, and `experiments/issue-12-highlight-probe.mjs`.\n\n4. **Errors and fixes**\n   - **Wrong selector.** `#source` doesn't exist; the panes are `#source-text` and `#target-text`.\n   - **`.field span` overrode `.hl-*`.** Its specificity let it override the highlight colours and shrink the code font. No theme file\nsits directly in `themes/` (they are `themes/material3/colors.lino`,\n`themes/classic/konard/glass.lino`, …), so the glob is empty and the production\nbundle contains:\n\n```js\nasync function GR(e){const n=new URL(Object.assign({})[`../themes/${e}`],import.meta.url); … }\n```\n\nEvery theme is fetched from `…/assets/undefined` and `loadTheme(id)` rejects with\n`Cannot load theme data: 404 …`. The theme files are not emitted into `dist/` either.\n\n## Reproduction\n\n1. A Vite app that calls `loadTheme('glass')` from `@link-foundation/ui-themes`.\n2. `vite build` and serve `dist/`.\n3. `loadTheme` rejects; the bundle contains `Object.assign({})[\\`../themes/${e}\\`]`.\n\nScript: https://github.com/link-foundation/universal-translator/blob/35fca8d5b993d5b4146d6b7aaba3a71070556efe/experiments/issue-12-vite-theme-url.mjs\n(builds the demo without its workaround and prints the compiled `readThemeFile`).\n\n## Workaround used by the consumer\n\nA `pre` Vite transform rewrites the expression to a string concatenation, which\nVite leaves alone, and the `themes/` folder is copied next to the bundle:\n\n```js\ncode.replace(\n  'new URL(`../themes/${path}`, import.meta.url)',\n  \"new URL('../themes/' + path, import.meta.url)\"\n);\n// writeBundle: cpSync(node_modules/@link-foundation/ui-themes/themes, `${dir}/themes`)\n```\n\n(https://github.com/link-foundation/universal-translator/blob/35fca8d5b993d5b4146d6b7aaba3a71070556efe/examples/universal-app/vite.config.js)\n\n## Suggested fix\n\n- Build the URL in a way bundlers do not rewrite, e.g.\n  `new URL('../themes/' + path, import.meta.url)` or\n  `new URL(path, new URL('../themes/', import.meta.url))`, and document that the\n  `themes/` folder has to be served next to the module; or\n- Better for bundlers: make every theme loadable through a static import map\n  (`import.meta.glob('../themes/**/*.lino', { query: '?raw' })` is Vite-only, so\n  rather a generated `themes/index.js` with `() => import('./classic/konard/glass.lino.js')`\n  entries holding the text), so bundlers emit only the chosen themes.\n- Add an external Vite production-build smoke test that calls `loadTheme` (as asked\n  for the inspector assets in #212).\nEOF\ncat > docs/case-studies/issue-12/upstream/ui-tokens-theme-specificity.md <<'EOF'\n# ui-tokens: [REDACTED] theme CSS loses to a host's dark palette (skins apply in the light scheme only)\n\nSource: link-foundation/ui main (3d556e7), published `@link-foundation/ui-tokens@0.1.0`,\n`@link-foundation/ui-themes@0.2.0`.\nConsumer: link-foundation/universal-translator web demo.\n\n## What happens\n\n`compileThemeCss(theme)` writes every rule as\n`[data-theme=\"glass\"]:where(<scheme/contrast/motion selectors>)`. Because of `:where()`\neach rule has the specificity of one attribute, (0,1,0).\n\nAn app usually has its own palette for when no skin is chosen, written the common way:\n\n```css\n:root { --color-surface: #f6f7f4; }                                     /* (0,1,0) */\n@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {\n  :root:not([data-scheme='light']) { --color-surface: #141a18; }        /* (0,2,0) */\n}\n```\n\nIn the light scheme the skin wins only by source order (its `<style>` comes later).\nIn the dark scheme the host rule has (0,2,0) and wins whatever the order, so a skin\nseems to \"not work\" in dark mode: `data-theme=\"glass\"` is set and the skin's\nstylesheet is loaded, but `--color-surface` stays the app's `#141a18` instead of\nglass' `#0b1626`.\n\n## Reproduction\n\nhttps://github.com/link-foundation/universal-translator/blob/35fca8d5b993d5b4146d6b7aaba3a71070556efe/experiments/issue-12-skin-specificity.mjs\nloads the glass theme, compiles it and puts it after such a palette in Chromium:\n\n```\nbefore light: --color-surface #e9f2fa\nbefore dark: --color-surface #141a18   <- the app's palette, not the skin\nafter light: --color-surface #e9f2fa\nafter dark: --color-surface #0b1626\n```\n\n## Workaround used by the consumer\n\nScope the app's palette to \"no skin or the app's own skin\":\n\n```css\n:root:not([data-theme]), [data-theme='app'] { … }\n@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {\n  :root:not([data-theme]):not([data-scheme='light']),\n  [data-theme='app']:not([data-scheme='light']) { … }\n}\n```\n\n## Suggested fix\n\n- Document in ui-themes/ui-tokens how a host palette must be written next to a\n  compiled theme (scoped as above, or inside a lower cascade layer, or with `:where()`).\n- Optionally let `compileThemeCss(theme, { layer: 'theme' })` wrap its output in\n  `@layer`, so a host can order `@layer app-defaults, theme;` and never depend on\n  specificity or on the order of `<style>` elements.\n- A browser test with a host palette that has a dark-scheme rule.\nEOF\necho ok"

dependent details about anything in a language, we just specify a more concrete type, set or category.\\n\\nThat is the vision.\\n\\nWe should start by supporting full translation of something simple once we take top 20-30 most used programming languages and support parsing all of them into meta language and back (basic roundtrip CST survival), we should also support translation from meta language expression to meta language expression, where we still in meta language, yet convert one abstraction to another (equivalent translation, with different levels of abstractions), yet at the same time we support exactly all concepts of each such language separately.\\n\\nFor example we can have function with no return value and no argument in both C, C#, C++ and so on, they match 1 to 1.\\n\\nYet we clearly have dependent expressions in languages, for example in `printf(\\\"Hello World!\\\\n\\\");` we have `printf` function depended on its import via `#include <stdio.h>`.\\n\\nYet effect of `printf(\\\"Hello World!\\\\n\\\");` is equivalent to effect of `System.Console.WriteLine(\\\"Hello, World!\\\");`.\\n\\nYet main function C depends only on file, yet in C# function depends also on class.\\n\\nSo if we select configuration of translation as `same effect` we do `meta language` -> `meta language` translation/transformation first, and only after we translatated from C expression in `meta language` to equivalent expression  of C# `meta language` we can do materialization or formatting or translation from meta language to C#.\\n\\nIf `literal` translation configuration we can preserve source code comments, yet for example in `context dependent` translation we may also parse comments in natural language and transform them accordingly.\\n\\n```\\n/* Hello world in C */\\n\\n#include <stdio.h>\\n\\nmain()\\n{\\n    /* print \\\"Hello World!\\\" into console followed by new line symbol by function call */\\n    printf(\\\"Hello World!\\\\n\\\");\\n}\\n```\\n\\ngoes to\\n\\n```\\n/* Hello World in C# */\\nclass HelloWorld\\n{\\n    static void Main()\\n    {\\n        /* print \\\"Hello World!\\\" into console followed by new line symbol by method call */\\n        System.Console.WriteLine(\\\"Hello, World!\\\");\\n    }\\n}\\n```\\n\\nFor example here we clearly updated the comment with C replaced to C#, `function call` -> `method call` and so on.\\n\\nSo by default we should use context dependent translation, with multiple configuration options like I described.\\n\\nOnce we finish with stabilization of translation between hello world programs, we should stabilize translation between all rosetta code examples.\\n\\nWe start by implementing our translator in JavaScript and Rust at the same time.\\n\\nWe should have just enough source code in both languages (we do manual translation first in this pull request), yet it should be perfect.\\n\\nFor that we should use our github.com/link-foundation/meta-language and github.com/link-foundation/relative-meta-logic and https://github.com/link-assistant/router/pull/775 to do general universal translation tool, yet our universal translator itself will be used in meta-language tooling, and relative-meta-logic tooling as well.\\n\\nWe should take bast practices from https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/228, https://github.com/link-foundation/relative-meta-logic/pull/184 and https://github.com/link-assistant/router/pull/775, so we can create best possible and fully configurable universal translation core, it should have best possible architecture, with everything configurable, everything replaceable, decoratable (based on decorator pattern) and so on.\\n\\nYet in this pull request we focus on core architecture and simple hello world and rosetta code, we can modify examples in such a way, that we get the most perfect ones, which illustrate all our principles, so we have perfect examples we can build up on in top 20-30 languages, if any examples are missing in original we craft them perfectly. We focus on best possible readability - use full english words for functions/methods/variables and so on, and maximum simplicity, each algorithm should be correct in principle and work, but be as simple as possible, yet in such form that will be easy to translate between these.\\n\\nWe also should support multiple layers of translation rules.\\n\\nIdeally in the future, it should be possible to prove that translation is equivalent in some narrow set of translation requirements, for example effect of code in programs in both languages can be the same.\\n\\nAlso it should be possible in future make full deep translation not only a code of application, but also the code of standard libraries and other libraries and so on.\\n\\nEven if we only have binaries, we can still translate asm to C# CIL or Java ByteCode and so on (by the way we should also have these examples) for translation between different version of asm and CIL and byte code and so on, all again via meta language.\\n\\nAnd we also can have an option to provide common library implementation, meaning we first implement library in both languages, translate C code to meta language, replace only function calls to common library implementation, check that it compiles, and runs exactly the same, after that we also use that common library and implement it C#, and after that we can simplify translation from C to C# via meta language by using common library, that means translation will be nearly line to line translation.\\n\\nAnd so on, so I genuinely don't agree with impossibility of translation using only rules.\\n\\nThere also may be transformation/translation rules specific to repository/project/organization, we also may have translation or tranformation in the same language but changing only style or for example translate C# code and russian comments to C# code and English comments and so on. So there may be lots of configuration options as well as custom transformation/translation rules.\\n\\nWe also can change style when translating from one style of javascript to specific (non traditional) style of C# and so on.\\n\\nSo our architecture should use best of https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/main/docs/associative-tech-stack.md, and do it in the most extensible and configurable way, so it is always easy to extend/replace/workaround in any possible way.\\n\\nWe need to collect data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), list of each and all requirements from the issue, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).\\n\\nPlease plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\",\"comments\":[],\"title\":\"A tool to do translation between languages\"}",

[2026-11-25T17:01:27.084Z] [INFO]         "content": "1\t=== PR 5\n2\tUniversal translator: 32 programming languages (with Lean and Rocq), machine code, 30+ controlled natural languages, fragments, CLI/API/Docker and web demo\n3\tFixes #1\n4\t\n5\t## Summary\n6\t\n7\tThis PR adds a translator for programs. It does not match templates: it reads source text with per-language grammar tables and rewrites it through rules. It translates between **32 programming languages** (including **Lean 4** and **Rocq**), **three machine targets** (NASM x86-64, CIL, JVM/Jasmin) and **controlled versions of 30+ natural languages**. The JavaScript (`js/`) and Rust (`rust/`) implementations write byte-identical output for every golden translation.\n8\t\n9\t```text\n10\tsource ──parser──▶ source tree ──understanding rules──▶ meta ──type inference──▶ typed meta\n11\t  ──meaning rules──▶ ──custom layers──▶ ──context rules──▶ ──emitter──▶ target text\n12\t  ──lowering──▶ stack machine ──▶ NASM / CIL / JVM (Jasmin)\n13\tNASM / CIL / JVM ──reader──▶ stack machine ──lifting──▶ meta\n14\tcontrolled natural text ──reader──▶ meta ──writer──▶ controlled natural text\n15\t```\n16\t\n17\t### Requirements gate (test-driven)\n18\t\n19\t`docs/case-studies/issue-1/requirements.lino` lists every requirement from the issue and its comments. `docs/case-studies/issue-1/rosetta-coverage.lino` lists the Rosetta Code algorithm types. `scripts/check-requirements.mjs` checks each requirement against the repository; for example, it compares the language lists of both implementations and checks that every task has a golden in every language. It fails CI (`Rust and cross-language translation` job, and `js/tests/requirements.test.js` under Node, Bun and Deno) unless every requirement is **done** or **blocked with a written reason**.\n20\t\n21\tThe gate caught real gaps during this work. The Rust implementation was missing 10 languages; that was fixed and the gate now passes.\n22\t\n23\t### Web demo\n24\t\n25\t![Web demo translating a Python function to Rust](https://github.com/link-foundation/universal-translator/blob/issue-1-35d65b774bf6/docs/screenshots/web-demo.png?raw=true)\n26\t\n27\t`examples/universal-app` is a React demo in which any programming or natural language can be translated to any other. You can paste a whole program, one function or one statement. The `web-e2e` job in `.github/workflows/example-app.yml` drives it in Chromium (`examples/universal-app/e2e/translate.e2e.mjs`) and takes the screenshot above.\n28\t\n29\t### Fragments: statements, functions or a whole program\n30\t\n31\t`translateFragment` / `parseFragment` (JS) and `translate_fragment` / `parse_fragment` (Rust), plus `universal-translator translate --fragment`, accept a statement, one or more functions, or a whole program. Each comes back as the same kind of fragment in the target. A fragment only has to be complete: a function must end with its closing. Otherwise the translator fails with the reason and the line, for example `The fragment is not complete: it ends before its closing (line 2)`. Goldens for every language are in `examples/programs/fragments/translated/` and are checked by `write-fragments.mjs --check`.\n32\t\n33\t### CLI, library, HTTP API and Docker\n34\t\n35\t- `universal-translator serve` starts an HTTP API (`GET /languages`, `POST /translate`). It reads `--port`/`--host`, then `PORT`/`HOST`, then `.lenv`, through lino-arguments.\n36\t- `js/src/index.js` (with types) and the `rust/` crate are the libraries.\n37\t- The `Dockerfile` image runs the CLI and the server. The release workflow builds it and smoke tests the CLI and the HTTP API.\n38\t\n39\t### Source layout and best practices\n40\t\n41\t- Sources are split into `src/meta` (shared types and trees), `src/formal` (programming languages, Lean, Rocq and machine code) and `src/natural` (human languages, with a reader and a writer), in both `js/` and `rust/`. The `source-layout` check rejects imports that point outwards from the meta layer.\n42\t- [`docs/case-studies/issue-1/best-practices.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/universal-translator/blob/issue-1-35d65b774bf6/docs/case-studies/issue-1/best-practices.md) maps the associative technology stack, the code architecture principles and all 17 CI/CD best practices to evidence, or gives a reason when one does not apply. `cargo clippy -D warnings` now runs in CI.\n43\t- **Test coverage is required by CI.** `npm run test:coverage` replaces `npm test` in the Node.js job. It fails below 94% line, 91% branch or 95% function coverage of `js/src` and `bin`; current coverage is 95.4%, 92.1% and 96.5%. The Rust crate runs the same goldens, but CI does not measure its coverage.\n44\t\n45\t### Programming languages (32) and machine code\n46\t\n47\t| | |\n48\t| --- | --- |\n49\t| Languages | JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Ruby, Lua, PHP, C, C++, C#, Java, Go, Rust, Kotlin, Swift, Perl, Dart, Scala, Julia, R, Groovy, Objective-C, Nim, D, Pascal, Fortran, Ada, Visual Basic .NET, Bash, MATLAB/Octave, Zig, **Lean 4, Rocq** |\n50\t| Dialects | Pascal, Fortran, Ada, VB.NET, Bash, MATLAB/Octave and Zig have their own program layout. block` | `js/src/meta/notation.js`, `rust/src/meta/notation.rs`: one line per node, children nested, no block lines, `otherwise` for the second branch | `js/tests/meta-notation.test.js`, `rust/tests/grammar.rs`, `issue-12-meta-parity.sh` (13 example programs, JS = Rust) |\n| 10 | The whole codebase and all earlier issues and PRs delivered | Audit of issues 1, 6 and 8 against the code, below | See \"Audit of earlier issues\" |\n| 11 | Skins do not work: find out why, report upstream | `styles.css` palette scoped to the app skin; panel radius, opacity and blur from the theme tokens; Monaco takes the skin colours | E2E `changesTheSettings` (glass changes the panel in light and dark); `issue-12-skin-specificity.mjs`; link-foundation/ui#292, link-foundation/ui#293 |\n| 12 | Case study with data, timeline, requirements, root causes, solutions | This folder | — |\n| 13 | Debug output where data is missing | `examples/universal-app/src/debug.js`: `?debug` or localStorage `universal-translator.debug=1`; the CLIs already have `--trace` | Manual |\n| 14 | Issues in other repositories reported with repro, workaround and fix | link-foundation/ui#292, link-foundation/ui#293 | — |\n| 15 | Apply everything to the whole codebase (JS and Rust alike) | Meta view and rules in both; the CLIs alike | Parity scripts and tests in both |\n\n## Root Causes\n\n### The title and the inputs jumped\n\nMeasured before the work (`data/before-layout-shift.json`, 1280×900):\n\n- The note of a random example (\"Function: …\") wrapped onto its own line and pushed the pickers\n  32 px down.\n- A picker changed width (188 ↔ 322 px) when its version select appeared or disappeared, so the\n  pickers moved sideways.\n- Each pane grew with its own text: the source and the translation started at different heights\n  (593 vs 536 px) and had different heights (318 vs 375 px).\n\nThe fix gives every row a fixed height whatever its content: the example note sits on a line of its own\nheight, the version select keeps its place (disabled when there is none), and the two panes share one\ngrid row that grows with the longer text between 260 px and 70% of the window, then scrolls.\n\n### Skins did not work\n\nTwo independent causes:\n\n1. **Specificity of the app palette.** `compileThemeCss` writes every skin rule as\n   `[data-theme=\"glass\"]:where(…)`, specificity (0,1,0). The app's own palette was `:root` in the\n   light scheme (0,1,0: the skin won by order only) and `:root:not([data-scheme='light'])` in the\n   dark scheme (0,2,0: the app always won). So skins applied in the light scheme and not in the dark one\n   (`before-glass-dark.png`). `experiments/issue-12-skin-specificity.mjs` reproduces it in Chromium:\n   `before dark: #141a18` against `after dark: #0b1626`. The fix scopes the palette to\n   `:root:not([data-theme]), [data-theme='app']`.\n   Reported as link-foundation/ui#293 (document it, or let `compileThemeCss` write to a `@layer`).\n2. **Shapes were not taken from the skin.** Even with the colours right, the panels kept their 8 px\n   corners and an opaque card: the CSS used fixed values. They now come from the theme tokens\n   (`--surface-radius`, `--ui-control-corner`, `--surface-opacity`, `--surface-blur`), with the\n   app's values when a theme has none.\n\nA third cause had been worked around before this issue, but it was never reported: in a Vite build,\n`loadTheme` of ui-themes fetches `…/assets/undefined`. Vite compiles\n``new URL(`../themes/${path}`, import.meta.url)`` into a one-level glob that is empty\n(`experiments/issue-12-vite-theme-url.mjs` prints\n``new URL(Object.assign({})[`../themes/${e}`], import.meta.url)``). Reported as link-foundation/ui#292.\n\n### `body: block` in the meta language\n\nThe meta view wrote every child under its field name (`condition:`, `then:`, `value:`) and every block\nas `main: block` / `statements`. In Links Notation `name:` names a link, which is meant to be unique, but\nthese field names repeat on every line. The meta program itself needs neither: the kind of a node says\nwhat its children are (an `if` has a condition, then a block, then optionally another). Before and after,\nfor one Python `if`/`else`:\n\n```\nprogram                                   program\n  main: block                               if\n    statements                                binary greater (type boolean)\n      if                                        name x\n        condition: binary (operator greater)    number 1 (type integer)\n          left: name (name x)                 print (newline true)\n          right: number (value 1)               text big (type text)\n        otherwise: block                      otherwise\n          statements                            print (newline true)\n            print (newline true)                  text small (type text)\n              value: text (value small)\n        then: block\n          statements\n            print (newline true)\n              value: text (value big)\n```\n\nBlocks are not written; a second block is introduced by one plain word (`otherwise`). `--json` keeps the\nfull structure for programs that need the field names.\n\n### JSON for rules, standards and settings\n\nRules were a JSON object (`--rules rules.json`, the server's `rules` field, the demo's text box);\nsaved standards and word standards were JSON in localStorage. Settings were already Links Notation\n(ui-settings). Rules are now indented Links Notation:\n\n```\noutput:\n  (find console.log) (replace print)\nnames:\n  (find total) (replace sum)\n```\n\nThe readers still accept JSON when a text starts with `{` (or `[` for stored standards), so nothing\nsaved earlier is lost.\n\n### Highlighting: problems found on the way\n\n- The demo's `.field span` rule (specificity 0,1,1) overrode the `.hl-*` colour classes. It now\n  applies only to the field's own label.\n- Monaco's `setTheme` writes `<style>` into `<head>`; a MutationObserver on `<head>` that repainted\n  the theme looped forever. It now reacts to the skin's own `#ui-theme` stylesheet only, and\n  `applySkin` sets a theme only when its colours changed.\n- `color-mix(in oklab, …)` computes to `oklab(…)`, which Monaco cannot read (it took it as black).\n  The colours are converted to `#rrggbb` by painting one canvas pixel.\n- Natural languages write names in their own words (`gcd-of` is `gcd-из` in Russian): the\n  highlighter asks the writer (`writeName`) for the written form of every name of the meta program.\n- Words with combining marks (Bengali `লেখো`) were split: the word pattern now includes `\\p{M}`.\n- A pane whose translation failed has no lexicon; Monaco's tokenizer crashed on it. Such a pane is now\n  plain text.\n- Python tuple assignment (`a, b = b, a % b`) is not read by the translator\n  (`Unexpected \",\" after statement`). While such a text is typed, the highlighter keeps the names of\n  the last text that it could read.\n\n## Solutions And Alternatives\n\n| Need | Chosen | Alternatives considered |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Code editor | Monaco (`monaco-editor` 0.58, ESM, loaded only when chosen; only the features a pane uses are imported) | CodeMirror 6 (smaller, already a dependency of ui-components; it would need its own tokenizer too); a plain textarea stays the default |\n| Highlighting | Our own: the words of the meta program the translator reads (names, functions, values) and the comment/quote marks of the language description; one highlighter for the plain panes and for Monaco (`highlightLine` is a Monaco tokens provider) | TextMate grammars (Shiki), Prism, highlight.js, Tree-sitter: a grammar per language (32 programming and 30 natural ones), and they know nothing of the meta language |\n| Equal panes that grow | CSS grid row with `align-items: stretch`, `field-sizing: content` for the textarea, min/max heights; Monaco reports its content height | JavaScript measuring both panes on every change |\n| Skins | Scope the app palette to the app skin; shapes from the theme tokens | Load the app palette in a lower `@layer` (needs the skin in a layer too, see ui#293) |\n| Storage | Indented Links Notation (`links-notation` already a dependency) with JSON still read | JSON (what the issue asks to move away from) |\n| Debug output | `?debug` in the demo; `--trace` in the CLIs | — |\n\nOnline references:\n\n- Vite: `new URL(url, import.meta.url)` and how template literals become globs:\n  https://vite.dev/guide/assets.html#new-url-url-import-meta-url\n- CSS specificity of `:where()` (zero) and `:is()`/`:not()` (their argument):\n  https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/CSS/:where\n- Cascade layers: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/CSS/@layer\n- `field-sizing`: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/CSS/field-sizing\n- Monaco tokens providers (`setTokensProvider`, `IState`):\n  https://microsoft.github.io/monaco-editor/typedoc/functions/languages.setTokensProvider.html\n\n## Audit Of Earlier Issues\n\nAUDIT_PLACEHOLDER\n\n## Debugging\n\n- Demo: open it with `?debug` (or set localStorage `universal-translator.debug` to `1`). Every\n  translation, detection, highlighting, skin and editor step is written to the console with its timing.\n- CLIs: `translate … --trace` prints every pipeline stage; `meta <language> --json` prints the full\n  meta program.\n"

| — |\n| 15 | Apply everything to the whole codebase (JS and Rust alike) | Meta view and rules in both; the CLIs alike | Parity scripts and tests in both |\n\n## Root Causes\n\n### The title and the inputs jumped\n\nMeasured before the work (`data/before-layout-shift.json`, 1280×900):\n\n- The note of a random example (\"Function: …\") wrapped onto its own line and pushed the pickers\n  32 px down.\n- A picker changed width (188 ↔ 322 px) when its version select appeared or disappeared, so the\n  pickers moved sideways.\n- Each pane grew with its own text: the source and the translation started at different heights\n  (593 vs 536 px) and had different heights (318 vs 375 px).\n\nThe fix gives every row a fixed height whatever its content: the example note sits on a line of its own\nheight, the version select keeps its place (disabled when there is none), and the two panes share one\ngrid row that grows with the longer text between 260 px and 70% of the window, then scrolls.\n\n### Skins did not work\n\nTwo independent causes:\n\n1. **Specificity of the app palette.** `compileThemeCss` writes every skin rule as\n   `[data-theme=\"glass\"]:where(…)`, specificity (0,1,0). The app's own palette was `:root` in the\n   light scheme (0,1,0: the skin won by order only) and `:root:not([data-scheme='light'])` in the\n   dark scheme (0,2,0: the app always won). So skins applied in the light scheme and not in the dark one\n   (`before-glass-dark.png`). `experiments/issue-12-skin-specificity.mjs` reproduces it in Chromium:\n   `before dark: #141a18` against `after dark: #0b1626`. The fix scopes the palette to\n   `:root:not([data-theme]), [data-theme='app']`.\n   Reported as link-foundation/ui#293 (document it, or let `compileThemeCss` write to a `@layer`).\n2. **Shapes were not taken from the skin.** Even with the colours right, the panels kept their 8 px\n   corners and an opaque card: the CSS used fixed values. They now come from the theme tokens\n   (`--surface-radius`, `--ui-control-corner`, `--surface-opacity`, `--surface-blur`), with the\n   app's values when a theme has none.\n\nA third cause had been worked around before this issue, but it was never reported: in a Vite build,\n`loadTheme` of ui-themes fetches `…/assets/undefined`. Vite compiles\n``new URL(`../themes/${path}`, import.meta.url)`` into a one-level glob that is empty\n(`experiments/issue-12-vite-theme-url.mjs` prints\n``new URL(Object.assign({})[`../themes/${e}`], import.meta.url)``). Reported as link-foundation/ui#292.\n\n### `body: block` in the meta language\n\nThe meta view wrote every child under its field name (`condition:`, `then:`, `value:`) and every block\nas `main: block` / `statements`. In Links Notation `name:` names a link, which is meant to be unique, but\nthese field names repeat on every line. The meta program itself needs neither: the kind of a node says\nwhat its children are (an `if` has a condition, then a block, then optionally another). Before and after,\nfor one Python `if`/`else`:\n\n```\nprogram                                   program\n  main: block                               if\n    statements                                binary greater (type boolean)\n      if                                        name x\n        condition: binary (operator greater)    number 1 (type integer)\n          left: name (name x)                 print (newline true)\n          right: number (value 1)               text big (type text)\n        otherwise: block                      otherwise\n          statements                            print (newline true)\n            print (newline true)                  text small (type text)\n              value: text (value small)\n        then: block\n          statements\n            print (newline true)\n              value: text (value big)\n```\n\nBlocks are not written; a second block is introduced by one plain word (`otherwise`). `--json` keeps the\nfull structure for programs that need the field names.\n\n### JSON for rules, standards and settings\n\nRules were a JSON object (`--rules rules.json`, the server's `rules` field, the demo's text box);\nsaved standards and word standards were JSON in localStorage. Settings were already Links Notation\n(ui-settings). Rules are now indented Links Notation:\n\n```\noutput:\n  (find console.log) (replace print)\nnames:\n  (find total) (replace sum)\n```\n\nThe readers still accept JSON when a text starts with `{` (or `[` for stored standards), so nothing\nsaved earlier is lost.\n\n### Highlighting: problems found on the way\n\n- The demo's `.field span` rule (specificity 0,1,1) overrode the `.hl-*` colour classes. It now\n  applies only to the field's own label.\n- Monaco's `setTheme` writes `<style>` into `<head>`; a MutationObserver on `<head>` that repainted\n  the theme looped forever. It now reacts to the skin's own `#ui-theme` stylesheet only, and\n  `applySkin` sets a theme only when its colours changed.\n- `color-mix(in oklab, …)` computes to `oklab(…)`, which Monaco cannot read (it took it as black).\n  The colours are converted to `#rrggbb` by painting one canvas pixel.\n- Natural languages write names in their own words (`gcd-of` is `gcd-из` in Russian): the\n  highlighter asks the writer (`writeName`) for the written form of every name of the meta program.\n- Words with combining marks (Bengali `লেখো`) were split: the word pattern now includes `\\p{M}`.\n- A pane whose translation failed has no lexicon; Monaco's tokenizer crashed on it. Such a pane is now\n  plain text.\n- Python tuple assignment (`a, b = b, a % b`) is not read by the translator\n  (`Unexpected \",\" after statement`). While such a text is typed, the highlighter keeps the names of\n  the last text that it could read.\n\n## Solutions And Alternatives\n\n| Need | Chosen | Alternatives considered |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Code editor | Monaco (`monaco-editor` 0.58, ESM, loaded only when chosen; only the features a pane uses are imported) | CodeMirror 6 (smaller, already a dependency of ui-components; it would need its own tokenizer too); a plain textarea stays the default |\n| Highlighting | Our own: the words of the meta program the translator reads (names, functions, values) and the comment/quote marks of the language description; one highlighter for the plain panes and for Monaco (`highlightLine` is a Monaco tokens provider) | TextMate grammars (Shiki), Prism, highlight.js, Tree-sitter: a grammar per language (32 programming and 30 natural ones), and they know nothing of the meta language |\n| Equal panes that grow | CSS grid row with `align-items: stretch`, `field-sizing: content` for the textarea, min/max heights; Monaco reports its content height | JavaScript measuring both panes on every change |\n| Skins | Scope the app palette to the app skin; shapes from the theme tokens | Load the app palette in a lower `@layer` (needs the skin in a layer too, see ui#293) |\n| Storage | Indented Links Notation (`links-notation` already a dependency) with JSON still read | JSON (what the issue asks to move away from) |\n| Debug output | `?debug` in the demo; `--trace` in the CLIs | — |\n\nOnline references:\n\n- Vite: `new URL(url, import.meta.url)` and how template literals become globs:\n  https://vite.dev/guide/assets.html#new-url-url-import-meta-url\n- CSS specificity of `:where()` (zero) and `:is()`/`:not()` (their argument):\n  https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/CSS/:where\n- Cascade layers: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/CSS/@layer\n- `field-sizing`: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/CSS/field-sizing\n- Monaco tokens providers (`setTokensProvider`, `IState`):\n  https://microsoft.github.io/monaco-editor/typedoc/functions/languages.setTokensProvider.html\n\n## Audit Of Earlier Issues\n\nAUDIT_PLACEHOLDER\n\n## Debugging\n\n- Demo: open it with `?debug` (or set localStorage `universal-translator.debug` to `1`).                                                                                                                                                                           | Parity scripts and tests in both                                                                                                                      |\n\n## Root Causes\n\n### The title and the inputs jumped\n\nMeasured before the work (`data/before-layout-shift.json`, 1280×900):\n\n- The note of a random example (\"Function: …\") wrapped onto its own line and pushed the pickers\n  32 px down.\n- A picker changed width (188 ↔ 322 px) when its version select appeared or disappeared, so the\n  pickers moved sideways.\n- Each pane grew with its own text: the source and the translation started at different heights\n  (593 vs 536 px) and had different heights (318 vs 375 px).\n\nThe fix gives every row a fixed height whatever its content: the example note sits on a line of its own\nheight, the version select keeps its place (disabled when there is none), and the two panes share one\ngrid row that grows with the longer text between 260 px and 70% of the window, then scrolls.\n\n### Skins did not work\n\nTwo independent causes:\n\n1. **Specificity of the app palette.** `compileThemeCss` writes every skin rule as\n   `[data-theme=\"glass\"]:where(…)`, specificity (0,1,0). The app's own palette was `:root` in the\n   light scheme (0,1,0: the skin won by order only) and `:root:not([data-scheme='light'])` in the\n   dark scheme (0,2,0: the app always won). So skins applied in the light scheme and not in the dark one\n   (`before-glass-dark.png`). `experiments/issue-12-skin-specificity.mjs` reproduces it in Chromium:\n   `before dark: #141a18` against `after dark: #0b1626`. The fix scopes the palette to\n   `:root:not([data-theme]), [data-theme='app']`.\n   Reported as link-foundation/ui#293 (document it, or let `compileThemeCss` write to a `@layer`).\n2. **Shapes were not taken from the skin.** Even with the colours right, the panels kept their 8 px\n   corners and an opaque card: the CSS used fixed values. They now come from the theme tokens\n   (`--surface-radius`, `--ui-control-corner`, `--surface-opacity`, `--surface-blur`), with the\n   app's values when a theme has none.\n\nA third cause had been worked around before this issue, but it was never reported: in a Vite build,\n`loadTheme` of ui-themes fetches `…/assets/undefined`. Vite compiles\n``new URL(`../themes/${path}`, import.meta.url)`` into a one-level glob that is empty\n(`experiments/issue-12-vite-theme-url.mjs` prints\n``new URL(Object.assign({})[`../themes/${e}`], import.meta.url)``). Reported as link-foundation/ui#292.\n\n### `body: block` in the meta language\n\nThe meta view wrote every child under its field name (`condition:`, `then:`, `value:`) and every block\nas `main: block` / `statements`. In Links Notation `name:` names a link, which is meant to be unique, but\nthese field names repeat on every line. The meta program itself needs neither: the kind of a node says\nwhat its children are (an `if` has a condition, then a block, then optionally another). Before and after,\nfor one Python `if`/`else`:\n\n```\nprogram                                   program\n  main: block                               if\n    statements                                binary greater (type boolean)\n      if                                        name x\n        condition: binary (operator greater)    number 1 (type integer)\n          left: name (name x)                 print (newline true)\n          right: number (value 1)               text big (type text)\n        otherwise: block                      otherwise\n          statements                            print (newline true)\n            print (newline true)                  text small (type text)\n              value: text (value small)\n        then: block\n          statements\n            print (newline true)\n              value: text (value big)\n```\n\nBlocks are not written; a second block is introduced by one plain word (`otherwise`). `--json` keeps the\nfull structure for programs that need the field names.\n\n### JSON for rules, standards and settings\n\nRules were a JSON object (`--rules rules.json`, the server's `rules` field, the demo's text box);\nsaved standards and word standards were JSON in localStorage. Settings were already Links Notation\n(ui-settings). Rules are now indented Links Notation:\n\n```\noutput:\n  (find console.log) (replace print)\nnames:\n  (find total) (replace sum)\n```\n\nThe readers still accept JSON when a text starts with `{` (or `[` for stored standards), so nothing\nsaved earlier is lost.\n\n### Highlighting: problems found on the way\n\n- The demo's `.field span` rule (specificity 0,1,1) overrode the `.hl-*` colour classes. It now\n  applies only to the field's own label.\n- Monaco's `setTheme` writes `<style>` into `<head>`; a MutationObserver on `<head>` that repainted\n  the theme looped forever. It now reacts to the skin's own `#ui-theme` stylesheet only, and\n  `applySkin` sets a theme only when its colours changed.\n- `color-mix(in oklab, …)` computes to `oklab(…)`, which Monaco cannot read (it took it as black).\n  The colours are converted to `#rrggbb` by painting one canvas pixel.\n- Natural languages write names in their own words (`gcd-of` is `gcd-из` in Russian): the\n  highlighter asks the writer (`writeName`) for the written form of every name of the meta program.\n- Words with combining marks (Bengali `লেখো`) were split: the word pattern now includes `\\p{M}`.\n- A pane whose translation failed has no lexicon; Monaco's tokenizer crashed on it. Such a pane is now\n  plain text.\n- Python tuple assignment (`a, b = b, a % b`) is not read by the translator\n  (`Unexpected \",\" after statement`). While such a text is typed, the highlighter keeps the names of\n  the last text that it could read.\n\n## Solutions And Alternatives\n\n| Need                  | Chosen                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Alternatives considered                                                                                                                                              |\n| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| Code editor           | Monaco (`monaco-editor` 0.58, ESM, loaded only when chosen; only the features a pane uses are imported)                                                                                                                                          | CodeMirror 6 (smaller, already a dependency of ui-components; it would need its own tokenizer too); a plain textarea stays the default                               |\n| Highlighting          | Our own: the words of the meta program the translator reads (names, functions, values) and the comment/quote marks of the language description; one highlighter for the plain panes and for Monaco (`highlightLine` is a Monaco tokens provider) | TextMate grammars (Shiki), Prism, highlight.js, Tree-sitter: a grammar per language (32 programming and 30 natural ones), and they know nothing of the meta language |\n| Equal panes that grow | CSS grid row with `align-items: stretch`, `field-sizing: content` for the textarea, min/max heights; Monaco reports its content height                                                                                                           | JavaScript measuring both panes on every change                                                                                                                      |\n| Skins                 | Scope the app palette to the app skin; shapes from the theme tokens                                                                                                                                                                              | Load the app palette in a lower `@layer` (needs the skin in a layer too, see ui#293)                                                                                 |\n| Storage               | Indented Links Notation (`links-notation` already a dependency) with JSON still read                                                                                                                                                             | JSON (what the issue asks to move away from)                                                                                                                         |\n| Debug output          | `?debug` in the demo; `--trace` in the CLIs                                                                                                                                                                                                      | —                                                                                                                                                                    |\n\nOnline references:\n\n- Vite: `new URL(url, import.meta.url)` and how template literals become globs:\n  https://vite.dev/guide/assets.html#new-url-url-import-meta-url\n- CSS specificity of `:where()` (zero) and `:is()`/`:not()` (their argument):\n  https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/CSS/:where\n- Cascade layers: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/CSS/@layer\n- `field-sizing`: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/CSS/field-sizing\n- Monaco tokens providers (`setTokensProvider`, `IState`):\n  https://microsoft.github.io/monaco-editor/typedoc/functions/languages.setTokensProvider.html\n\n## Audit Of Earlier Issues\n\nThe earlier issues (1, 6 and 8) and their pull requests were read again against the code, the\nCLIs were run in shell pipes, and both CLIs were compared on the same inputs. All 34 CI checks pass on the latest commit, nobody has commented on the issue or the PR, and `main` is merged in. Its description has \"Fixes #12\", a table mapping each requirement to its code and tests, before/after screenshots, and the audit results.\n\n**What issue 12 asked for:**\n- **Demo layout:** the title and inputs stay put whatever the text length, and both panes are always the same height.\n- **Editor and view options:**\n  - an optional Monaco editor (loaded only when picked in the settings), with highlighting driven by our meta language;\n  - a word-wrap switch;\n  - a separate Rules tab;\n  - \"How it works\" moved below the translator;\n  - controls aligned.\n- **No JSON by default:** rules, language standards and settings are stored as indented Links Notation, in both the JavaScript and Rust versions. JSON saved earlier is still read. `coverage` and `detect` also print Links Notation now, and `--json` gives JSON.\n- **Meta view:** no more `body: block` or `field:` labels; each node is one line with its children nested under it. JavaScript and Rust print the same output for all 13 example programs.\n- **Skins:** they now work in the dark scheme too, and in the desktop build. The two causes are in the `ui` library and are reported there as link-foundation/ui#292 and link-foundation/ui#293, with repros and suggested fixes. Both are still open, so this repo works around them.\n- **Case study and debugging:** the case study is in `docs/case-studies/issue-12`. Opening the demo with `?debug` writes what it does to the console.\n\n**Audit of earlier issues 1, 6 and 8:**\n- **Fixed here:**\n  - The JavaScript CLI crashed in shell pipes, both when input arrived late and when the reader closed early.\n  - `coverage` and `detect` printed JSON by default.\n- **Not done in this PR:** a set of gaps that are each a translation-coverage or Rust-port task of its own, the kind issue 8 tracks. Each is listed with evidence in the case study and the PR description. The larger ones:\n  - the meta language has whole numbers only, so `7 / 2` becomes `Math.trunc(7 / 2)`;\n  - JavaScript arrow functions and classes aren't read;\n  - only 39.4% of Rosetta Code lines are read;\n  - the Rust CLI has no `serve`.\n\n  Because of these, the issue's \"no undelivered requirements left\" across all earlier issues is not fully met.\n\n**CI fixes after merging `main`:**\n- **Bundle size limit:** `main`'s web build now fails on any warning, and Monaco's core (about 1.5 MB) can't be split under the 500 kB chunk warning limit. I raised Vite's limit above Monaco and added a check that fails the build if any other chunk passes 500 kB. A forced test confirmed it catches an oversized chunk and ignores Monaco.\n- **CLI pipe tests:** `main` requires every test to be registered unconditionally. The two pipe tests now register on all runtimes and show as skipped, with the reason, under Bun and Deno, because the pipeline runs the CLI with Node.\n- **ShellCheck:** fixed a warning in the JS/Rust parity script."

When standard input isn't ready yet, `readFileSync(0)` throws `EAGAIN` (for example `(sleep 1; echo 'print(1)') | universal-translator translate python javascript -`), and a reader that closes early (`| head`) caused an unhandled `EPIPE`. Now `readStandardInput` waits through `EAGAIN`, and `EPIPE` ends the CLI quietly. The test `js/tests/cli-pipes.test.js` uses real shell pipes; it fails before the fix and passes after.\n- **P9**: `coverage` and `detect` printed JSON by default, against requirement 8. They now print indented Links Notation in both CLIs; `--json` still prints JSON.\n\nNot done in this PR. These are known gaps in translation coverage or the Rust port, each a separate task of the kind issue 8 tracks; the case study lists each with evidence:\n- B2: the meta language has integers only, so `7 / 2` becomes `Math.trunc`.\n- B3: `translate-program` needs the Meta Language 1.0 module.\n- P1: some natural-language wordings aren't read.\n- P2: comments are translated word by word.\n- P3: the concrete syntax tree doesn't keep whitespace inside expressions.\n- P4: few language versions.\n- P5: no Wikidata words in Rust.\n- P6: no ranking step.\n- P7: Rosetta Code coverage is 39.4% of lines.\n- P10: the Rust CLI has no `serve`.\n- P12: no Hello World Collection corpus.\n- JavaScript arrow functions and classes aren't read.\n\n## Screenshots\n\nBefore (from the issue, and the glass
